newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses break records, gold and oil dip.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses break records, gold and oil dip.

text.p: The London stock market hit record highs on Thursday after fears eased of higher interest rates and Frankfurt and Paris also scaled new peaks as European bourses recovered from Wednesday's late profit-taking.

Wall Street, the world's biggest stock market, weighed in with solid gains in morning trading in New York. The Dow Jones industrial average advanced more than 50 points, boosted by good corporate earnings news.
Recovering from a shaky opening, the London market, Europe's busiest, climbed with bonds on news of slower inflation and the maintenance of British interest rates at six percent for now.
Wall Street's rebound gave it extra support but, while registering a gain of 0.9 percent on the day, it stalled just short of the 4,200 level on the key FTSE 100 share index.
"The market's just incredible," said one London share trader. "Obviously the inflation data helped and the pressure on interest rates has been relieved."

Gold, weakened recently by competition from a firmer dollar and booming stock markets plus concern over central bank gold sales, edged lower. Oil also declined after a weather-related spike upwards on Wednesday.

On the currency markets, the dollar gained against the mark but slipped against the yen. Analysts had expected some consolidation following a recent move above 1.60 marks and to a 46-month high against the yen.
The dollar firmed against the mark after Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said the German economy was in a grave position and the bank could not ignore this.
On balance, economists had not expected a British interest rate rise yet despite the Bank of England's known desire for higher rates to contain inflationary risks.
But surprisingly strong British jobless data on Wednesday, with unemployment falling to a six-year low, had raised a few doubts and jangled market nerves.

The London stock market opened a little easier on Thursday. But it was then reassured by news that inflation slowed to 2.5 percent last month from November's 2.7 percent and the decision to keep interest rates unchanged.
Insurance shares also rose on talk of takeover bids.
French stocks, too, hit a record high close, up 0.8 percent, and remained in bullish mood despite the Bank of France's failure to trim interest rates, as had been hoped.
The French central bank's monetary council meeting, which left rates unchanged, was the first since the appointment of two new members seen to lean more towards faster rate cuts.
Frankfurt also rewrote the record books, closing floor trade at a record for the DAX index just short of the 3,000 level. Dealers said the rally was not over yet.
"The champagne bottles will be out," said one trader. "There is more in this market. The uptrend is definitely still there."
The Amsterdam, Copenhagen and Oslo bourses were others which climbed into record territory.
Gold, however, slipped from the previous close to below $354 an ounce amid concern that other central banks might follow the Dutch and sell more of their gold reserves, traders said.
"In the coming months and years, European central banks will gradually reduce their gold reserves," one Zurich trader said.
World oil prices, which had recovered in late trade on Wednesday amid concern over cold U.S. weather, also eased.
London February futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend were down 21 cents at $23.63 a barrel after an earlier low of $23.44.

Elsewhere, the Bank of Spain made a cut of a quarter point to six percent in its key money rate, surprising markets despite the peseta's strength and benign inflation. The peseta responded by strengthening to 83.49 to the mark from 83.70 overnight.
CURRENCIES LATE IN EUROPE
The dollar was quoted around 116.55 yen and 1.5955 marks, compared with 117.17 and 1.5912 late on Wednesday.
Sterling, after weakening on the interest rate news, revived to around 2.6745 marks from 2.6701 overnight. The French franc showed little reaction at 3.3748 to the mark versus 3.3754.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 38.6 points higher at a record close of 4,197.5, just short of an earlier all-time high of 4,198.9.

Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 4.86 at a new closing high of 2,993.31 after an all-time record of 2,998.61 earlier. The IBIS DAX for electronic trade was up 19.56 at 2,996.12 after a record 2,998.79 earlier.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 19.79 at its highest ever close of 2,407.77 but just short of its all-time peak of 2,418.93, hit on Wednesday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed London business around $353.35 versus an afternoon fix of $353.05 and previous close of $354.15. Silver added around three cents to $4.73.
